messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: gpu-autoscale-prod - autoscaler errors + queue growth in inference-prod (us-west-2). Paging @oncall-sre and infra team. Root cause unknown; initial metric: pending queue ~2.3k, 95th latency elevated.

sara: I'm oncall, looking now. Any obvious deploys?

james: No big deploys from deploy-bot in the last 30m. I see repeated autoscaler errors in control-plane logs.

maya: paste logs from autoscaler (tail):
```
autoscaler: attempt_scale_up failed: error="no compatible node: fragmented MIG topology, cannot place MIG slices"
event: PodPending: "0/120 nodes are available: 97 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 23 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate." 
placer: MIG_ALLOC_FAIL node=gpu-node-42 slice=1/4 stranded=true
```

alec: Confirming. Scheduler reports binpacking failures due to different MIG slice sizes across nodes -> a lot of small slices are stranded and can't accept current request profiles. Autoscaler tries to scale but hits placement constraints and scale-limit (provider-side) as well.

oncall-sre: Initial impact assessment: ~8 customers reporting 500s and 429s via CS channel, +platform metrics show tail latency + error rate up. Marking S2 -> escalate if not recovered in 30m.

sara: Immediate mitigation options: 1) evict low-priority training/async jobs to free whole-GPU nodes for inference, 2) launch new homogeneous nodes with matching MIG config and remove fragmented ones, 3) route heavy customers to fallback model-variant (cpu/quantized) while we rebalance.

james: I'll start evicting low-priority pods. Running:
```
# evict low priority inference pods
kubectl -n inference delete pod -l workload=async,priority=low --grace-period=0 --force
```

maya: I'll open a manual scale request with cloud team to add 6 nodes with 4xMIG-1g profile (to match typical requests). If cloud can't provision immediately, we fallback to routing policy.

oncall-sre: Doing on-call handoff to alec for next 2 hours. @alec you'll take lead for mitigation.

alec: Ack. I'll restart the autoscaler after eviction to clear transient errors and trigger manual scale once new nodes are provisioning. Also going to apply a temporary scheduler policy to prefer consolidation: add node affinity for inference-critical pods to nodes labeled `inference-consolidate=true`.

maya: Manual scale request submitted (ticket #CLOUD-2121). Cloud responded: "can add nodes but quota hit on GPU slices in us-west-2; request requires quota increase and node replacement to avoid fragmentation". ETA unknown.

james: Trying a local trick to free MIG-able GPUs: draining a handful of nodes with small leftover slices to coalesce. Commands:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-42 && kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```

ops: Heads-up: draining will cause evictions and more 5xxs for affected workloads; coordinate with CS on which customers to notify.

customer-success: CS notes: 3 enterprise tenants (TENANT-A, TENANT-B, TENANT-C) seeing elevated failures; we're routing support messages but need ETA for mitigation to share.

alec: To address stranded MIG slices long-term: plan to standardize MIG profiles per node pool (e.g., all nodes in pool use 1g slices for inference), run a background rebalancer to consolidate pods onto appropriately sized nodes, and enforce admission control to reject mismatched requests. But short-term we need capacity.

deploy-bot: autoscaler pod restarted by alec at 2003456798.

james: After evictions + drains queue depth dropped from 2.3k -> 680 within 9 minutes. Errors dropped but still above baseline.

oncall-sre: Noted. Still seeing ~15% of requests hitting 429s for heavy token workloads.

maya: Cloud increased quota for GPU slices (approved). New nodes provisioned but some existing nodes still have mismatched MIG partitions, so autoscaler still can't place all pods. I'm coordinating a rolling replace to build a homogeneous node pool.

alec: Running rebalancer plan: mark old fragmented pool `legacy-frag=true`, cordon, create new pool with `mig=1g` and `inference-consolidate=true`, then migrate critical pods. This should un-strand slices.

ops: For immediate customer relief, we've enabled routing rule to divert 20% of traffic for affected tenants to quantized model variant (increased latency but fewer GPUs). Patch applied at 2003456822.

customer-success: Customers notified: initial ETA for stable relief 20-30m, we've provided temporary mitigation notes.

james: Monitoring: queue now 210, 95th latency trending down, error rate ~2% above baseline.

oncall-sre: Good. Keep monitoring for 1 hour after queue stabilizes. If no regression, downgrade severity.

maya: New homogeneous pool is 50% up; autoscaler placements succeeding on new nodes. Early signs show stranded slices being reclaimed.

alec: Postmortem notes to capture: autoscaler should surface clearer errors (fragmentation vs quota), add automatic small-job preemption policy, and enforce node-pool MIG homogeneity in autoscaler placement rules.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: RECOVERY: queue stabilized and autoscaler placements restored at 2003456840. Monitoring to continue. Incident annotated S2 -> resolved if stable.

ops: Leaving a follow-up task for infra to schedule a maintenance window to standardize MIG configs and run a binpack rebalance job.

alec: Thanks team. Handoff complete, I'm updating the incident doc and opening postmortem.

customer-success: Thanks, sharing postmortem timeline with customers. :thumbsup:
